title: Invoice Status
prompt: A TypeScript billing screen needs a simple status label. Write a function that returns "paid" if the invoice is paid, "overdue" if its dueDate is before today, and "open" otherwise. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD strings.

explanation.beginner:
Example: invoiceStatus({"dueDate":"2026-01-01","paid":true}, "2026-02-01") produces "paid". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “detects overdue invoices”: input [{"dueDate":"2026-01-01","paid":false},"2026-02-01"] produces "overdue". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “detects overdue invoices”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
